newsitem.title: JAPAN: Sumitomo to cut executive pay over scandal.
newsitem.headline: Sumitomo to cut executive pay over scandal.

text.p: Sumitomo Corp president Kenji Miyahara said on Wednesday that the company will reduce its executives' salaries for six months over a recent scandal involving unauthorised copper trades.
Miyahara told reporters his own salary will be cut by about 40 percent, but did not specify the amount by which other executives' salaries would be cut.
The cuts will be effective from April salary payments, he said.
Miyahara was speaking to reporters after a monthly meeting of Sumitomo group companies in Osaka, western Japan.

Asked whether Sumitomo executives will take any responsibility for the scandal involving rogue copper trader Yasuo Hamanaka, Miyahara said : "I think the best way to show that executives bear some responsibility is for their salaries to be cut."
He added that he hopes to make a formal announcement on the issue "very soon".

On Sumitomo's internal investigation into how such a scandal happened in the company, Miyahara said he is hoping to complete the investigation and reveal its results by the company's next board meeting on June 27.
"But I cannot comment at this time how much I will be able to disclose from the findings," he added.

Hamanaka was fired from the company last June after generating a loss of $2.6 billion in unauthorised copper trades. He has pleaded guilty to fraud and forgery, and his trial is continuing in a Tokyo court.
